source: Bank of Japan, Flow of Funds Accounts, financial assets by sector, instrument 140 (Japanese transferable deposits): amounts outstanding FOF_FFAS<sector>A140 and transactions FOF_FFAF<sector>A140, quarterly, flat file fof2_en.zip; rows are the finest sectors that add up to all holders (sector 700), with a sector's figure minus its listed parts where they leave something out; figures before 2005 are on the 1993 SNA basis
note: Every owner is a sector of the Bank of Japan's flow of funds, the Bank's own count of who holds all of it, in yen. Foreign investors are owners who live outside Japan. Net bought is the Bank's quarterly transactions; price and other changes is the change in holdings minus what was bought, which is the reconciliation the Bank publishes. The Bank changed its accounting basis in the first quarter of 2005, so a window that includes that quarter carries the change in price and other changes. Source: Bank of Japan. Transferable deposits are deposits that can be drawn on at once, as the Bank of Japan records them. This book is money, so it is not added into the world ledger's total of owned wealth.
